transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2029-10-02
Start time: 15:00 UTC
Duration: ~62 minutes
Attendees: Jordan Hayes (Redwood AE), Priya Nair (Redwood SE), Alex Mercer (Peregrine Head of Platform), Nora Kim (Peregrine Security), Samir Patel (Peregrine Cloud Networking)

Summary: Intro / discovery focused on cross-account private connectivity patterns for Redwood Private. Discussed PrivateLink vs Transit Gateway, account onboarding, IP overlap mitigation, regional constraints (eu-west-1 and us-east-1), KMS/encryption questions, and SOC 2 / audit log expectations. Agreed to share diagrams, checklist, and schedule detailed network workshop.

[00:00] Jordan Hayes: hey everyone thanks for joining, this is Jordan from Redwood, um gonna kick off, we have Priya our solutions engineer as well, quick roundtable can folks say where they're dialling in from?
[00:12] Alex Mercer: alex here, i'm in boston, head of platform at Peregrine Labs, we run a hybrid cloud stack, lots of services in aws and we have a few onprem pockets still.
[00:19] Nora Kim: nora, security at peregrine, san francisco.
[00:22] Samir Patel: samir, cloud networking, seattle but i'm traveling — i'll be on and off.
[00:26] Priya Nair: priya, se in redwood, focused on private deployments and networking. great to meet you all.

[00:35] Jordan Hayes: great, agenda real quick: 1) understand your current topology and constraints, 2) walk through private connectivity options for redwood (privatelink, vpc peering, transit gateway patterns), 3) compliance/networking asks, 4) next steps. sound ok?
[00:48] Alex Mercer: yep that's perfect. our main driver: we want to run some sensitive PII workloads through a hosted inference endpoint but with private networking so data never traverses public internet. evaluating redwood private vs dedicated. cost is a factor but security and residency are showstoppers.

[01:05] Priya Nair: quick clarifying q: when you say "hosted inference endpoint" do you mean your app will call Redwood's private deployment in our account or you're evaluating redwood-hosted with private peering?
[01:16] Alex Mercer: good point — we want Redwood to be in our AWS environment. so private control plane or private deployment — basically redwood's service in our VPCs. we also want cross-account connectors because our infra spans multiple aws accounts.

[01:30] Samir Patel: and to add, we have stricter egress rules in eu-west-1 — some workloads can't leave eu-west-1, and some teams use us-east-1. we'll need multi-region account mapping.

[01:42] Jordan Hayes: understood. let me give a quick high-level on options: 1) PrivateLink-based model where we publish an endpoint service in your account (service consumer/producer pattern) — basically private endpoints for API calls; 2) VPC peering if it's single-account and CIDR non-overlapping; 3) Transit Gateway / TGW when you need many-to-many connectivity across accounts and regions. each has tradeoffs on scaling, manged IPs, and egress.

[02:10] Nora Kim: question — with privatelink, does data decrypt on the redwood side? we have KMS controls and need customer-managed keys.
[02:18] Priya Nair: good q — so in our private deployment we support integrating with customer KMS for at-rest keys (we'll supply PE to manage artifact storage). for in-flight traffic it's TLS over the private link; logs and audit can be exported to your account — we can use your KMS for storage encryption depending on the artifact (we have a few modes). i can follow up with specifics.

[02:38] Alex Mercer: to clarify — can we hold the KMS keys entirely? we have an HSM; we prefer to keep control.
[02:44] Priya Nair: yes customers can bring keys; for on-prem packages we'd integrate with customer HSM/KMS — for VPC-based private deployments we can support CMK usage for S3 artifact stores and DB encryption. i'll flag this as action item with our infra doc.

[03:02] Samir Patel: network first: our accounts are split like: prod account in eu-west-1 VPC 10.0.0.0/16, staging in us-east-1 10.1.0.0/16, some legacy onprem with overlapping 10.0.0.0/16 — ip overlap is a pain. how have others solved this?

[03:18] Priya Nair: common patterns: 1) TGW with route maps + NVA to rewrite, 2) use PrivateLink which avoids peering and IP overlap by proxying traffic through the ENI in the consumer account, or 3) ask customers to NAT/translate — not ideal. PrivateLink is popular when you can't modify CIDRs.

[03:40] Alex Mercer: we prefer not to change CIDRs. sounds like PrivateLink could be the one. any limits? throughput / number of connections?

[03:48] Jordan Hayes: PrivateLink scales but there are ENI and connection limits per AZ, and there's an additional cost for endpoints. For high-throughput inference we'll typically recommend Dedicated capacity with PrivateLink, or alternatively TGW with peering if you can manage CIDRs. Priya, maybe run numbers — latency and cost delta.

[04:05] Priya Nair: yes i'll pull our performance profiles. quick note — for token-heavy workloads, cross-AZ hops add ms; if you put the redwood serving nodes in the same region and leverage local endpoints, latency is minimal. we have customers who've used PrivateLink in the same region with sub-40ms p95. but depends on model size and batching.

[04:28] Samir Patel: oh interesting — we care about p95 under 200ms for chat flows. 40ms would be great. are there published perf pages?
[04:34] Jordan Hayes: we have a model perf catalogue — i'll share the link after. one caveat — if you route across regions (eu->us) you'll incur added latency and potential residency issues.

[04:45] Nora Kim: residency: our legal says any EU regulated PII must remain in eu-west-1 and logs retained per GDPR. does redwood support region-locked deployments?
[04:54] Priya Nair: yes we can pin deployments to a region in our private offering. we also provide audit log export to your S3 bucket in the same region; RBAC and SSO are supported via SAML/SCIM. for deeper compliance packages (ISO, SOC 2), we have an enterprise add-on.

[05:12] Alex Mercer: perfect. what about cross-account onboarding — we have many accounts; onboarding overhead needs to be small.

[05:21] Priya Nair: onboarding pattern we've used: central shared TGW + delegated VPC attachments, or PrivateLink with an automation script we provide that creates endpoints across accounts using a CloudFormation/Cloud Development Kit. we can automate account whitelisting using your org map. we have templates.

[05:42] Samir Patel: automation is key. can we see that template? also, for private endpoints we need control over which subnets the ENIs land in (for security groups and routing) — is that configurable?

[05:53] Priya Nair: you can choose subnets for endpoints; our CFN lets you specify target subnets and SGs, yes. i'll include the template.

[06:00] Alex Mercer: on egress — we route outbound model downloads through our NAT; is there any outbound traffic from redwood to public? like telemetry?
[06:08] Jordan Hayes: by default we minimize outbound egress in private deployments; telemetry can be routed to your S3 or exported to a metrics endpoint in your account. there's a small control-plane callback for billing/heartbeats which can be routed over the private link. we can avoid public internet egress if needed.

[06:25] Nora Kim: audit logs — we need immutable logs for six years and access logs for api calls. retention and tamper evidence, is that supported?
[06:33] Priya Nair: we push logs to your bucket with object-lock if you require WORM retention; we also have an audit pipeline into your SIEM (e.g., splunk, datadog). we can sign logs for tamper detection. i'll capture the specifics in the compliance pack.

[06:50] Jordan Hayes: shifting to deployment topology, do you envision a single shared redwood deployment that serves multiple accounts, or per-account instances?
[06:58] Alex Mercer: suggestion so far is shared service deployed in a shared services account, with PrivateLink endpoints in consumer accounts. that reduces management overhead. but for high throughput we might want dedicated per-account capacity.

[07:12] Priya Nair: both are valid. shared control plane / per-tenant serving nodes is our common pattern. for strict isolation we can run a fully dedicated deployment per account or per environment. that's more expensive but gives full network and compute isolation.

[07:26] Samir Patel: latency implications between shared and dedicated?
[07:29] Priya Nair: shared can introduce cross-tenant routing overhead, but with proper placement (same region AZ affinity) it's negligible. dedicated reduces noisy neighbor risk. cost vs isolation tradeoff.

[07:44] Alex Mercer: can we do a pilot in staging to measure latency and cost?
[07:48] Jordan Hayes: yes — typical path: 2-week pilot, we stand up a staging deployment in your account, run your prompt set, and produce latency and cost metrics. we'll need account IDs, sample traffic, and a small dataset for eval.

[07:59] Nora Kim: security review: we'll need SOC 2 type II report and pen test results and, additionally, SAML metadata for SSO. can you send those?
[08:08] Jordan Hayes: yes — i'll attach SOC2, pen test summary, and our SAML SSO guide. some docs are gated by NDA but we can share summaries.

[08:17] Alex Mercer: we also want IP allowlist templates and an example security group matrix.
[08:22] Priya Nair: included in the checklist i'll send.

[08:26] Samir Patel: network nit: do you support AWS RAM and resource shares for TGW attachments? we prefer central TGW in shared services.
[08:34] Priya Nair: yes TGW via RAM is supported — we can attach our VPC into your TGW or attach our SGW as a consumer depending on model. for cross-region we can use TGW peering or regional endpoints.

[08:46] Alex Mercer: do you have constraints around NAT Gateway egress IP aliasing? we need predictable egress IPs for partner allowlists.
[08:53] Jordan Hayes: we can assign static egress IPs via NATs in your account, or route egress through a dedicated egress VPC; we'll document options.

[09:01] Nora Kim: compliance again — where do artifacts (model weights, cached prompts) live? inside our S3? or in redwood-managed buckets?
[09:09] Priya Nair: for private deployments we can store artifacts in your S3 bucket; for hosted shared tenants we use our managed storage. for full control, request 'bring-your-own-buckets' during onboarding.

[09:19] Alex Mercer: ok, great. on the commercial side — how do billing and quotas work when the deployment is in our account?
[09:27] Jordan Hayes: two main models: 1) usage billing via Redwoods invoice for managed service, or 2) bring-your-own-infra with a platform fee — we can adapt. for confined private deployments we usually do committed Dedicated pricing plus a monthly platform fee. i'll include sample T&Cs.

[09:43] Samir Patel: one more technical: for private endpoints, are connections initialized from consumer to provider only? any chance of inbound connections into our account?
[09:52] Priya Nair: PrivateLink is consumer-initiated; we don't open arbitrary inbound. For callbacks we use the established connection or push metrics into your account. no open inbound SSH or admin plane.

[10:05] Alex Mercer: ok thanks. can we run through a quick checklist of items you need from us to spin up a pilot?
[10:11] Jordan Hayes: sure — 1) account IDs and role for cross-account automation, 2) VPC CIDRs and desired subnets for endpoints, 3) sample traffic and prompt set, 4) SOC2/PDR access if needed for docs, 5) any IP allowlist requirements.

[10:25] Alex Mercer: we'll compile. Samir will pull CIDRs and account IDs.
[10:29] Samir Patel: yep i'll send that by monday.

[10:33] Priya Nair: action note: i'll draft two topology diagrams (PrivateLink shared service pattern and TGW many-to-many) and an estimated cost/latency table. Jordan will produce the pilot statement of work.

[10:45] (cross talk, inaudible for a few seconds)

[10:50] Nora Kim: quick question — do you support private endpoints for model fine-tuning artifacts? we may want to fine-tune models on-prem and keep weights private.
[10:59] Priya Nair: yes for managed fine-tuning we can keep artifacts in your S3 or we can provide an on-prem agent that ships the training jobs to a private cluster; depends on your security needs. i'll include options.

[11:12] Jordan Hayes: wrapping up — recap and next steps: 1) Jordan: share SOC2, perf catalog, and pricing deck (by EOD 2029-10-02) 2) Priya: share CFN endpoint template, two topology diagrams, and preliminary latency/cost estimates (by 2029-10-07) 3) Alex/Samir: confirm account IDs, VPC CIDRs, and staging traffic sample (by 2029-10-05) 4) schedule a 90-minute network workshop with Peregrine cloud team (target week of 2029-10-08).

[11:45] Alex Mercer: that works. one ask — can you also include a quick runbook for rollback if we need to cut over?
[11:52] Priya Nair: yes we'll add a rollback playbook to the pilot SOW.

[11:58] Jordan Hayes: awesome, thanks everyone. any final q's?
[12:02] Nora Kim: just send the audit retention and object lock doc, thanks.
[12:06] Jordan Hayes: will do. thanks all, we'll follow up in email with the artifacts and the calendar invite for the network workshop.

End of transcript.

Follow-up notes (auto): Pilot SOW requested; prioritize PrivateLink staging pilot in eu-west-1; include BYOK/KMS options and object-lock configuration for audit logs.
